decisive_items: right femoral aplasia and left femoral hypoplasia
Right unilateral cleft lip and palate
response.rationale: Femoral aplasia/hypoplasia combined with characteristic facial dysmorphism (cleft lip/palate, micrognathia, low-set ears) and limb contractures is the defining pattern of femoral hypoplasia-unusual facies syndrome. Oligohydramnios sequence could explain contractures and some facial compression features but not femoral aplasia or cleft lip/palate.

rejected.why: Micrognathia and cleft lip/palate are present, but Pierre Robin syndrome does not explain femoral aplasia/hypoplasia, elbow contractures, or rib flattening.
Abruptio placentae may cause growth restriction but cannot account for the specific skeletal malformations, especially femoral aplasia/hypoplasia and cleft lip/palate.
Oligohydramnios sequence can cause limb contractures and some facial deformation, but it does not cause true femoral aplasia/hypoplasia or cleft lip/palate.
